Interface ByteSource

Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface ByteSource
A readable source of bytes, such as a file or a URL, that opens a new stream each time it is read.

Unlike an InputStream, a source is not an open resource: it can be kept, passed around and read any number of times, and each read method opens a stream and closes it before returning. Only openStream() and openBufferedStream() leave a stream for the caller to close.

The only abstract method is openStream(), so a lambda makes a source: 

ByteSource source = () -> socket.getInputStream();
byte[] bytes = ByteSource.of(file).read();
String text = ByteSource.of(uri).asCharSource(StandardCharsets.UTF_8).read();

Implementations may override the other methods with faster ones, such as sizeIfKnown() for a source that knows its size without reading it.

Since:
0.1.1

    • of

      static ByteSource of(Path file, OpenOption... options)

      Returns:

    • of

      static ByteSource of(URL url)
      Returns a source that reads what a URL points to, such as a resource from Class.getResource(String).

      It is meant for local resources, such as those of the class path or files. It opens the URL with no timeout, so a remote server that stops responding blocks a read forever: for one, open a connection with timeouts in a source of your own.

      Parameters:
      url - the URL to read
      Returns:
      a source of the content at url

    • of

      static ByteSource of(URI uri)
      Returns a source that reads what a URI points to, through the URL it converts to. Like of(URL), it is meant for local resources: it opens the URL with no timeout.
      Parameters:
      uri - the URI to read
      Returns:
      a source of the content at uri
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if uri is not absolute, or has a scheme no URL protocol handler supports

    • concat

      static ByteSource concat(ByteSource... sources)
      Returns a source that reads several sources one after the other. Each source is opened only when the previous one is read to its end.
      Parameters:
      sources - the sources to read
      Returns:
      a source of the content of sources, in order

    • concat

      static ByteSource concat(Iterable<? extends ByteSource> sources)
      Returns a source that reads several sources one after the other. Each source is opened only when the previous one is read to its end. The sources are copied: later changes to sources have no effect.
      Parameters:
      sources - the sources to read
      Returns:
      a source of the content of sources, in order
